data.name: God Awe-full Clicker
data.detailed_description:
God Awe-Full Clicker is an Endless Dungeon Clicker/Idle game full of Greek Mythology and Epic Battles with RPG style aspects.

KEY FEATURES
  • Decimate your Enemies with a combination of Clicking and passive Damage!
  • Level up and unlock Skills and Classes to take your Hero in different directions.
  • Earn GodPower and Spend it on Divine Blessings to get stronger. No reincarnation necessary.
  • Craft, Upgrade, and Optimize your Armor!
  • Recruit Gods to your cause and find their Artifacts to give them more power!
  • Complete Quests, Collections, and Trophies.
  • Roll the in-game dice to get instant rewards!
  • Spend some downtime on the Companion Mini-game to earn more in-game rewards.
  • Find Golden Apples and choose from a series of powerful upgrades!
  • Don't want to break your mouse? Use the built in Auto-Clickers to click the enemy for Damage, or your Hero for Healing!
  • Still want to click even with those on? Right clicking can deal heavy damage, and clicking in an Ambush Maneuver can do 200%+ Click Damage!
  • Face many known or not so well known Greek Gods and Champions and kick all of their behinds.

The Greek Gods have taken an interest in you as a Gladiator renowned for your prowess in the Arena. Zeus himself has sent his other Gods to test your mettle and train you to see if you're worthy of being a Guardian of Olympus. Recruit these gods to your side and train with them as they set you in front of enemy and enemy, summoning Champions, and sometimes even other Gods to push your limits. Find their Artifacts to increase their powers and steal the GodPower from enemies to increase your own.
Forge armor to build up your strength and defenses, and spend your skill points to specialize your Gladiator!

Like many other Clicker genre games, in God Awe-Full Clicker, you click things! Click the enemy to deal damage, use your right mouse button to deal heavy damage, click in ambush maneuvers to deal even greater damage, click your Gladiator to heal him, or click one of the many menus to open them.

God Awe-Full Clicker provides a lot of customization to the way you play with in-depth systems for Armor Crafting, Skill Trees, Classes, Divine Blessings, and more.

reviews.review:
Well, the fact it's a clicker game is pretty obvious and it's not a thing that's affecting my review. Being a clicker game is not bad. However, this one certainly isn't a good clicker game and I'm going to give my reasons.

Pros:
1. The ancient Greece theme is kind of fun, even though here it's mostly about aesthetics. Kind of wish it was deeper, but still not bad.
2. Art (by clicker game standards) is pretty good.
3. Shame to admit, but leaderboard and daily rewards made a surprisingly good job at keeping me going.

Cons:
1. The insane amount of randomness. This game uses randomness in so many aspects that it becomes really annoying. Most of your abilities have a chance to be activated, every attack can crit, mutihit, multi-multi-hit, apply some effect, etc, etc, and then it can also be blocked, dodged, deal less damage, and the same goes for attacks from enemies. This alone causes a lot of randomness in fights, so that you can fight on a certain floor for a while and be okay with it, but then suddenly some amount of crits happens, some amount of heals do not happen and you suddenly lose. Not that it's much of a loss in progress but in idle game it means that you can't be sure, leaving your hero to fight, that it will be fine.
But that's not all because all premium rewards are rare. Random clickables - "urns" give rewards (aside from some small amount of money) randomly. And those random rewards include premium currency, on which I'll touch upon later.
There are also Rare urns that give better rewards and appear randomly, and Titan Urns that give huge rewards and appear randomly with a very low chance.
And also there are daily rewards that are random (and range from trash to amazing) and voucher treasures that are given for certain things, and those are literal roulette spin with rewards from atrocious to absolutely huge, with atrocious being the result 90% of the time.
2. The hugest problem for me, vague mechanics. Most of the descriptions for abilities are really vague. Say, there is an ability that gives a bonus to godpower but there is no saying if it's multiplicative or additive with other abilities. Or there's an abilitiy that gives 0.5% crit chance. Does it give flat + 0.5% to your crit chance or 0.5% of what you already have (say you have 50% crit chance, 0.5% of 50% would be 0.25%)? That's a huge difference. And, in fact, some abilities are multiplicative and some are additive and there's no saying which does which and thus how much of an effect it would have.  Active skills' tooltips don't reflect any change that passive abilities have over them.
The worst part of this vague and unexpained mechanics is "DPS". To this day I don't know if DPS in this game is just an average damage calculated based on gladiator's attacks or it's, in fact, an absolutely separate damage that happens in addition to them. If it's former then why there are abilities that state that they are increasing DPS? If latter then there was never any real indication about that. Also, you can't see the damage of gladiator attacks itself anywhere, only DPS, which makes things even harder to estimate.
3. A slow progression with almost no way to accelerate it.
- No presige system
Most idle games have a system designed exactly for that: once you slow down too much, you reset the geme with bonus. This one isn't one of them
- No offline progression
Offline progression can be a saving grace for even a very mediocre game because it subjectively reduces time between things happen in-game. This one doesn't have it. To progress, you have to keep the game running.
- Very little in terms of in-game goals and rewards.
Game is basically linear. You can't have any kind of goals or strategies, except for "trophy" system which gives a very negligeable bonus of 1% per trophy.
4. Very dependant on premium currency.
Premium currency is mostly meant to be bought for money. In-game sources are both very random and very scarce.
And just so it happens that absolute majority of exciting abilities and upgrades are bought for premium currency.
Combine that with how slow the progress is and you'll see that it can be more than a little frustrating.

All in all, it's not a game I would recommend to anyone. If you wand a good idle game, play Realm Grinder or Idle Wizard.
